64	func WithInvocation(invocation string, cmd tea.Cmd) tea.Cmd {
65		if invocation == "" || cmd == nil {
66			return cmd
67		}
68		return func() tea.Msg {
69			msg := cmd()
70			start, ok := msg.(StartMsg)
71			if !ok {
72				return msg
73			}
74			start.Invocation = invocation
75			return start
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// RefusedMsg says an invocation will not produce a run, and why.
80	//
81	// It is the sibling of StartMsg and lives beside it for that reason: between
82	// them they are everything an invocation can come to. A keypress needs no such
83	// message — the view puts the same sentence in its footer (Rule 130) — which is
84	// why Refuse returns nil for an empty invocation rather than a message nobody
85	// would route.
86	//
87	// Reason is the view's own Availability.Reason, so the sentence an agent reads
88	// is the one the header greys with and the footer prints. One calculation,
89	// three readers.
90	type RefusedMsg struct {
91		Invocation string
92		Reason     string
93	}
94	
95	// Refuse builds the message, or nothing at all for a keyboard launch.
96	func Refuse(invocation, reason string) tea.Cmd {
97		if invocation == "" {
98			return nil
99		}
100		return func() tea.Msg {
101			return RefusedMsg{Invocation: invocation, Reason: reason}
102		}
103	}
104	
105	// Start builds the message for work that does not depend on the context.
106	func Start(run Run, work tea.Cmd) tea.Cmd {
107		return StartInContext(run, func(string) tea.Cmd { return work })
108	}
109	
110	// StartCancellable builds the message for a run whose queue can be stopped —
111	// today the clone, whose pipeline is launched from Update and hands back its
112	// context there and then.
113	func StartCancellable(run Run, work tea.Cmd, cancel context.CancelFunc) tea.Cmd {
114		return func() tea.Msg {
115			return StartMsg{
116				Run:    run,
117				Work:   func(string) tea.Cmd { return work },
118				Cancel: cancel,
119			}
120		}
121	}
122	
123	// CancelOpenMsg asks the router to stop the open run of a kind (D3, D7).
124	//
125	// A kind rather than an identifier: a progressive run belongs to a screen that
126	// owns the display while it goes, so there is one at a time and the view can
127	// name it without holding a JobID — which is the registry state D1 keeps out of
128	// views.
129	type CancelOpenMsg struct {
130		Kind Kind
131	}
132	
133	// CancelOpen builds the message.
134	func CancelOpen(kind Kind) tea.Cmd {
135		return func() tea.Msg { return CancelOpenMsg{Kind: kind} }
136	}
137	
138	// CancelMsg asks the router to stop a run by identifier (D7).
139	//
140	// An identifier here, where CancelOpenMsg names a kind, and the difference is
141	// which view is asking. A launch site cannot hold a JobID — it would have to
142	// before the registry allocated one — but `:jobs` reads the identifier out of
143	// the snapshot it is already rendering, which is the run the cursor is on.
144	type CancelMsg struct {
145		ID JobID
146	}
147	
148	// Cancel builds the message.
149	func Cancel(id JobID) tea.Cmd {
150		return func() tea.Msg { return CancelMsg{ID: id} }
151	}
152	
153	// CancelItemMsg asks the router to stop one target of a run.
154	type CancelItemMsg struct {
155		ID     JobID
156		Target string
157	}
158	
159	// CancelItem builds the message.
160	func CancelItem(id JobID, target string) tea.Cmd {
161		return func() tea.Msg { return CancelItemMsg{ID: id, Target: target} }
162	}
163	
164	// StartInContext builds the message for work that writes into a context-scoped
165	// cache. The builder is called once, in Update, with the name the router
166	// stamped on the run — so every command it returns carries that name however
167	// long the batch runs.
168	func StartInContext(run Run, work func(contextName string) tea.Cmd) tea.Cmd {
169		return func() tea.Msg { return StartMsg{Run: run, Work: work} }
170	}
171	
172	// ChangedMsg carries what the registry holds to every view that might show it.
173	// It is the whole of the broadcast (D1): a view keeps its own copy of a
174	// snapshot rather than reading a pointer the router writes, so nothing is read
175	// from View() while something else is writing it.
176	//
177	// It is sent on two occasions, and they are different in nature: a transition —
178	// something actually happened — and a spinner tick, where only the frame moved.
179	// The receiver does not have to tell them apart, which is why there is one
180	// message and not two.
181	//
182	// It lives in this package rather than in the router's so that every view can
183	// name it without importing the router, which imports them.
184	type ChangedMsg struct {
185		// Runs is a copy, oldest first, every context included. Filtering on the
186		// current one is the view's business (D8, FilterContext).
187		Runs []Run
188	
189		// Frame is the current spinner frame, bare — no escape sequence. Rule 122:
190		// a table cell is measured before it is styled, so a styled frame of seven
191		// visible cells measures twenty-eight and is truncated inside its own
192		// escape, which then bleeds down the rest of the table.
193		Frame string
194	
195		// RenderedFrame is the same frame styled, which is what a footer takes
196		// (Rule 128 — measurement there goes through lipgloss.Width, which ignores
197		// escapes). The router fills both so the two readings of one frame cannot
198		// drift, and so this package needs to know nothing about styling.
199		RenderedFrame string
200	}
201	
202	// Running counts the runs in the snapshot that have not settled. It saves every
203	// receiver the same three lines.
204	func (m ChangedMsg) Running() int {
205		return len(Unfinished(m.Runs))
206	}
207

150		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
151		// Cut and TailStyle split a cell into two coloured runs instead of Style's
152		// one: Style colours the first Cut(item) cells of the *finished* text —
153		// already measured, truncated and padded to the column's width — and
154		// TailStyle colours the rest. Both nil (the ordinary case, every column but
155		// the containers load gauges and the workspaces Git Status) leaves Style covering the whole cell as
156		// before.
157		//
158		// This is not the gradient Rule 122 forbids: nothing styled is ever
159		// measured. Cut reads a plain, already-final string — the split happens
160		// after truncation, at the same point Style already does its colouring —
161		// so it is the same "measure first, colour after" order applied twice
162		// instead of once, not an exception to it. It stays two runs rather than an
163		// arbitrary list: neither caller (the load gauges, the workspaces Git
164		// Status cell) has needed more than two, and Cut, a
165		// bare integer, is cheaper to reason about than a slice of spans that only
166		// ever holds two elements.
167		//
168		// Dropped only for a row a view has coloured whole — error, busy, a CVE
169		// severity — for the same reason Style is: a two-run cell still needs its
170		// own reset between the runs, which that solid background cannot afford.
171		// The plain "normal" selection consults both: each run repaints
172		// ColorTableLineSelected and bold itself, the same per-cell repaint that makes a
173		// single-run selected cell safe, so a load gauge keeps its fill/track
174		// split under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's colour alone.
175		Cut       func(T) int
176		TailStyle func(T) lipgloss.Style
177		// Spans splits a cell into any number of coloured runs, left to right, over
178		// the *fitted* text (measured, truncated and padded first). Widths below 0
179		// count as 0, a zero-width span renders nothing, spans past the cell's width
180		// are clipped and the cells left after the last span take Style. A nil or
181		// empty result takes the one-run path. Spans takes precedence over
182		// Cut/TailStyle; a column declaring both is rejected by a source test.
183		// Like Cut, widths count runes, so the cell must hold single-width glyphs.
184		// Dropped, like Cut/TailStyle, on a row a view has coloured whole.
185		Spans func(T) []Span
186		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
187		// `.` skips it.
188		Less func(a, b T) bool
189		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
190		// not participate.
191		Search func(T) string
192	}
193	
194	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
195	type Config[T any] struct {
196		Columns []Column[T]
197		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
198		Tokens []components.FilterToken
199		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
200		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
201		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
202		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
203		SortColumn int
204		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
205		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
206		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
207		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
208		SortDesc bool
209		// Key identifies an item across rebuilds, and is what the busy set is held
210		// on. Nil switches the busy facility off entirely, which is the default:
211		// most tables have no action to run on a row.
212		//
213		// It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on this struct instead. Columns are
214		// built once, in New, and close over nothing — imageRow exists because of
215		// that — so a predicate here would have to close over the view's map of
216		// in-flight actions, which is the same trap. Separating the identity from
217		// the state is what avoids it, and it is also what lets IsBusy answer for an
218		// object whose row does not exist yet: the guard on a confirm path runs
219		// before anything is rebuilt.
220		//
221		// Keying on identity rather than a flag on the row is also what survives the
222		// periodic refresh, which replaces the items while an action is running.
223		Key func(T) string
224		// StatusColumn is the column whose cell the spinner replaces while a row is
225		// busy — the one that answers "what about this row". Ignored when Key is
226		// nil.
227		//
228		// That column must not be sortable: askFor reserves width(Title)+2 for a
229		// column carrying a Less, which is expensive for a glyph.
230		StatusColumn int
231		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
232		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
233		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
234		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
235		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
236		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
237	}
238	
239	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
240	type Model[T any] struct {
241		cfg   Config[T]
242		table table.Model
243		bar   components.FilterBar
244	
245		items []T
246		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
247		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
248		// ordering while the screen shows another.
249		visible []T
250	
251		// styles is what was last handed to the table. The rendering is this
252		// package's now (render.go) and bubbles keeps its copy unexported, so the
253		// styles have to be kept on this side to be readable at render time.
254		styles table.Styles
255		// preserveColumnColors is true when styles.Selected is the plain "normal"
256		// look (ColorTableLineSelected) rather than a view's own error/busy/severity
257		// override. Computed once in applyStyles, read per cell in cellStyle: it
258		// is what tells the two selected-row treatments apart without render.go
259		// having to know what a severity or a busy row is.
260		preserveColumnColors bool
261		// offset is the first visible row — the scroll window bubbles kept in its
262		// viewport. clampOffset owns it.
263		offset int
264	
265		// busy maps an item's Key to the label of the action running on it. Held
266		// here rather than in the view so that one answer — IsBusy — serves the
267		// rendering, the footer and the guard that stops a second command being
268		// issued for the same object.
269		busy map[string]string
270		// spinnerFrame is what a busy row's status cell shows. The frame lives here
271		// and the tick stays in the view: a spinner needs a Cmd, and this package
272		// returns none (Rule 110).
273		spinnerFrame string
274		spinnerIdx   int
275	
276		// natural is the widest text each column produces over the visible rows,
277		// header included. rebuild refreshes it because it is already walking every
278		// cell there; it costs one lipgloss.Width per cell and nothing else.
279		natural []int
280		// measured is the copy the solver reads — natural as of the last
281		// measurement *moment*. The two are separate because the moment is the
282		// whole design: SetItems cannot tell a periodic refresh from a change of
283		// population (both arrive the same way), and remeasuring on every tick
284		// would make the columns dance on their own. See Remeasure.
285		measured []int
286		// measuredOnce records that a non-empty population has been measured. The
287		// first one measures itself: without that a table stays at its MinWidths
288		// for the life of the view, and nothing on screen says why.
289		measuredOnce bool
290	
291		sortColumn int
292		sortDesc   bool
293		width      int
294	}
295	
296	// New builds a table from its configuration.
297	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
298		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
299		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
300			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
301		}
302		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
303	
304		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
305		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
306			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
307		}
308	
309		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
310		// A frame from the start: a table whose view never calls AdvanceSpinner —
311		// one rendered in the same frame the action began — would otherwise show an
312		// empty status cell, which reads as "nothing is happening".
313		m.AdvanceSpinner()
314		// Through setStyles rather than the table alone: a table rendered before
315		// anything calls applyStyles — one built and drawn in the same frame — would
316		// otherwise render with the zero Styles, which carries no cell padding and
317		// so lays out two cells narrower per column than every width was solved for.
318		m.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
319		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
320		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
321		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
322		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
323		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
324			m.sortColumn = -1
325			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
326			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
327			m.sortDesc = false
328		}
329		return m
330	}
331	
332	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
333	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
334	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
335	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
336	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
337		m.items = items
338		m.rebuild()
339		// The one measurement this package takes on its own initiative. Every other
340		// SetItems may be a two-second refresh, and a table that re-measured on
341		// those would reshuffle its own columns while the user reads it.
342		if !m.measuredOnce && len(m.visible) > 0 {
343			m.Remeasure()
344		}
345	}
346	
347	// Remeasure re-reads the widest value in each column and lays the table out
348	// again. Call it at the moments a *user* changed what the table holds — a tab
349	// change, a drill-down, an explicit refresh — and never on a timer.
350	//
351	// This package cannot tell those apart on its own: a periodic reload and a
352	// change of population both arrive through SetItems, so the view is the only
353	// thing that knows. The cost of getting it wrong in the quiet direction is
354	// stated rather than discovered: a value that grew between two measurements
355	// stays truncated until the next one.
356	func (m *Model[T]) Remeasure() {
357		m.measuredOnce = m.measuredOnce || len(m.visible) > 0
358		m.Resize(m.width, 0)
359	}
360	
361	// promote makes the current measurement the one the solver reads. Resize is the
362	// only caller: a resize is itself a measurement moment — the user just changed
363	// how much room there is, and the content has not moved — and routing every
364	// promotion through it is what keeps Remeasure to one line.
365	func (m *Model[T]) promote() {
366		m.measured = append(m.measured[:0], m.natural...)
367	}
368	
369	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
370	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
371	
372	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
373	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
374	
375	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
376	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
377	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
378		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
379		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
380			var zero T
381			return zero, false
382		}
383		return m.visible[cursor], true
384	}
385	
386	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
387	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
388	
389	// SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
390	// remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
391	// level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
392	func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
393		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
394			return
395		}
396		m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
397		m.afterCursorMove()
398	}
399	
400	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
401	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
402	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
403	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() {
404		m.table.GotoTop()
405		m.afterCursorMove()
406	}
407	
408	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
409	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
410	
411	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
412	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
413	
414	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
415	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
416	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
417		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
418			return true
419		}
420		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
421			if c.Search != nil {
422				return true
423			}
424		}
425		return false
426	}
427	
428	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
429	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
430	
431	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown. The window is re-clamped: a table
432	// that just got shorter can leave the cursor below its own last visible row.
433	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) {
434		m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1))
435		m.clampOffset()
436	}
437	
438	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
439	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
440	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
441		m.table.Focus()
442		m.afterCursorMove()
443	}
444	
445	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
446		m.table.Blur()
447		m.setStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
448	}
449	
450	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
451	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
452	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
453	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
454		m.width = width
455		m.promote()
456		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, width, m.measured)
457	
458		cols := m.table.Columns()
459		for i := range cols {
460			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
461			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
462		}
463		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
464		m.bar.Resize(width)
465		if height > 0 {
466			m.SetHeight(height)
467		}
468		m.afterCursorMove() // the selected row is pinned to this width
469	}
470	
471	// The sort arrows, and what they cost. Named because widths.go has to reserve
472	// room for them: a column's MinWidth is the view's statement about its content,
473	// and it knows nothing about two cells this package appends to the header.
474	const (
475		sortArrowAsc  = " ▲"
476		sortArrowDesc = " ▼"
477	)
478	
479	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
480	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
481		if i != m.sortColumn {
482			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
483		}
484		if m.sortDesc {
485			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowDesc
486		}
487		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowAsc
488	}
489	
490	// CycleSort advances the sort: the column's first direction (ascending, or
491	// descending when it is DescFirst), then the other, then on to the next
492	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
493	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
494	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
495		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
496		if len(sortable) == 0 {
497			return
498		}
499		switch {
500		case m.sortColumn < 0:
501			m.sortColumn = sortable[0]
502			m.sortDesc = m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].DescFirst
503		case m.sortDesc == m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].DescFirst: // first direction shown
504			m.sortDesc = !m.sortDesc
505		default:
506			next := m.nextSortable(sortable)
507			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = next, next >= 0 && m.cfg.Columns[next].DescFirst
508		}
509		m.rebuild()
510		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
511	}
512	
513	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
514	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
515	//
516	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
517	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
518	// a branch nothing can ever check.
519	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
520		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
521			return sortable[at+1]
522		}
523		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
524			return -1
525		}
526		return sortable[0]
527	}
528	
529	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
530		var out []int
531		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
532			if c.Less != nil {
533				out = append(out, i)
534			}
535		}
536		return out
537	}
538	
539	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
540	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
541	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
542	
543	// SetSort puts the sort back where the table opened, or anywhere else the view
544	// can name. It exists for the one thing CycleSort cannot express: the registry
545	// browser starts a new search from the default order, and advancing `.` around
546	// the cycle until it comes back is not that.
547	//
548	// A column that cannot be sorted by leaves the table unsorted rather than
549	// silently sorted by something else — the same invariant New settles, so that
550	// nothing downstream has to re-check it.
551	func (m *Model[T]) SetSort(column int, desc bool) {
552		if column < 0 || column >= len(m.cfg.Columns) || m.cfg.Columns[column].Less == nil {
553			column, desc = -1, false
554		}
555		m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = column, desc
556		m.rebuild()
557		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
558	}
559	
560	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
561	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
562	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
563	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
564		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
565			var cmd tea.Cmd
566			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
567			m.rebuild()
568			// A search that keeps only short values has to give the room back, or
569			// the filter buys nothing visually. It is a user action on a settled
570			// population, which is exactly a measurement moment.
571			m.Remeasure()
572			return cmd
573		}
574	
575		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
576		if !ok {
577			return nil
578		}
579		switch key.String() {
580		case "/":
581			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
582			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
583			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
584			if !m.Searchable() {
585				return nil
586			}
587			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
588		case ".":
589			m.CycleSort()
590		// No bare letter is navigation (§3.26). The vim aliases h/j/k/l/g/G are
591		// gone application-wide: home/end already covered g/G, and keeping j/k
592		// alone would leave the one exception that makes the rule unverifiable.
593		// The letters now belong to the action vocabulary — internal/ui/keymap.
594		case "up":
595			m.table.MoveUp(1)
596			m.afterCursorMove()
597		case "down":
598			m.table.MoveDown(1)
599			m.afterCursorMove()
600		case "pgup":
601			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
602			m.afterCursorMove()
603		case "pgdown":
604			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
605			m.afterCursorMove()
606		case "home":
607			m.table.GotoTop()
608			m.afterCursorMove()
609		case "end":
610			m.table.GotoBottom()
611			m.afterCursorMove()
612		}
613		return nil
614	}
615	
616	// ── Rows an action is running on ─────────────────────────────────────────────
617	//
618	// A row says two things at once: what the object *is*, and what is *happening*
619	// to it. They have different sources of truth — the state comes back from
620	// docker on the next refresh, the transition is this application's own
621	// knowledge — and different lifetimes. Sharing one glyph is the point; sharing
622	// one function would make every table re-implement the precedence, so the rule
623	// lives here and there is one of it: **busy wins over state**.
624	
625	// MarkBusy records that an action is running on the item with this key, and what
626	// to call it. Call it from Update, never from a Cmd (Rule 110).
627	//
628	// A no-op when the config declares no Key: without one there is nothing to
629	// match a row against, and silently keeping a label nothing can display would
630	// be worse than ignoring it.
631	func (m *Model[T]) MarkBusy(key, label string) {
632		if m.cfg.Key == nil || key == "" {
633			return
634		}
635		if m.busy == nil {
636			m.busy = make(map[string]string, 1)
637		}
638		m.busy[key] = label
639	}
640	
641	// ClearBusy forgets an action.
642	//
643	// It must be called on **every** outcome, the failures included. Clearing only
644	// on success leaves the row spinning for the life of the view, and — worse —
645	// hides the state it still has: a `docker stop` that failed has to read
646	// `running` again, not go on turning.
647	func (m *Model[T]) ClearBusy(key string) { delete(m.busy, key) }
648	
649	// IsBusy reports whether an action is running on this key.
650	//
651	// It answers for an object whose row does not exist yet, which is what makes it
652	// the guard on a confirm path: without it a second keypress on a slow removal
653	// issues a second command, and the second one fails with "no such object" on an
654	// operation that in fact worked.
655	func (m *Model[T]) IsBusy(key string) bool {
656		_, ok := m.busy[key]
657		return ok
658	}
659	
660	// BusyLabels returns what is running, sorted, for a view's footer line. Sorted
661	// because a map's order changes between frames and a footer that reshuffles
662	// itself is unreadable.
663	func (m *Model[T]) BusyLabels() []string {
664		if len(m.busy) == 0 {
665			return nil
666		}
667		out := make([]string, 0, len(m.busy))
668		for _, label := range m.busy {
669			out = append(out, label)
670		}
671		sort.Strings(out)
672		return out
673	}
674	
675	// AdvanceSpinner moves the frame shown on busy rows one step on. Views call it
676	// from the spinner tick they already run.
677	func (m *Model[T]) AdvanceSpinner() {
678		m.spinnerFrame = spinner.Dot.Frames[m.spinnerIdx%len(spinner.Dot.Frames)]
679		m.spinnerIdx++
680	}
681	
682	// busyLabel returns the action running on an item, and whether there is one.
683	func (m *Model[T]) busyLabel(item T) (string, bool) {
684		if m.cfg.Key == nil || len(m.busy) == 0 {
685			return "", false
686		}
687		label, ok := m.busy[m.cfg.Key(item)]
688		return label, ok
689	}
690	
691	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
692	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
693		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
694		m.rebuild()
695		m.Remeasure() // a toggle is a user action on a settled population
696	}
697	
698	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
699	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
700	
701	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
702	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
703		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
704	
705		// The natural widths are taken here because the cells are already being
706		// built: the measurement is a lipgloss.Width per cell on a walk that
707		// happens anyway. Promoting them to the solver is a separate decision
708		// (see Remeasure) — this only keeps the answer current.
709		//

50		// CIGradeable is decided at load, not per frame: it needs the repository's
51		// remote, which is a git call. An image is never gradeable — it has no
52		// pipeline — so its zero value is already the truth.
53		CIScore     *string
54		CIGradeable bool
55		// Misconfig is the misconfiguration verdict as the cache holds it, stored
56		// rather than the finished state for Sensitive's reason: the verdict is one
57		// calculation, in theme, and a row carrying it would be a second place able
58		// to disagree with the workspaces list.
59		Misconfig *scan.MisconfigSummary
60		ScannedAt time.Time
61		// Scanned is false between a ctrl+a purge and the scan that replaces it.
62		// The target is still known — it is the counts that are not.
63		Scanned  bool
64		Scanning bool
65		Failed   bool
66		// Display is the image reference with its registry prefix replaced by the
67		// configured alias, stamped by setInventory the way SpinnerFrame is — the
68		// rows arrive from a Cmd, which cannot read the configuration off the model
69		// (Rule 110), and a column function is built once and cannot either.
70		//
71		// Empty means nobody stamped it, and displayName falls back to Name: a row
72		// built by hand must stay readable rather than render an empty cell.
73		Display      string
74		SpinnerFrame string
75	}
76	
77	// inventoryColumnCritical is the column the inventory opens sorted by,
78	// descending: the target with the most critical findings is the one the view
79	// exists to surface.
80	//
81	// This is an index, so it follows the column order: Secrets slotted in
82	// between Target and CRIT. A stale value doesn't sort wrong, it doesn't sort
83	// at all anymore — `datatable` drops a direction that names no sortable
84	// column, and Secrets isn't one.
85	const inventoryColumnCritical = 3
86	
87	// kindIcon is what the glyph column shows: which of the two caches the row came
88	// from. It is a column of its own rather than a prefix inside Target, the way
89	// the workspaces and containers tables do it — an icon glued into a text cell
90	// spends the identifying column's width on something that is not the name, and
91	// a column that measures the name has to measure the glyph too.
92	func (t scanTarget) kindIcon() string {
93		if t.Kind == kindImage {
94			return theme.IconDocker
95		}
96		return theme.IconWorkspace
97	}
98	
99	// kindIconRole colours the glyph above. The repository shares the explorer's
100	// and the workspaces' role rather than declaring a third: the same object is
101	// listed by three views, and one colour for it is what a role is for.
102	func (t scanTarget) kindIconRole() theme.IconRole {
103		if t.Kind == kindImage {
104			return theme.IconRoleImage
105		}
106		return theme.IconRoleRepository
107	}
108	
109	// shortName is what the Target column shows: the image reference with its
110	// registry prefix folded to the configured alias, or the repository path with
111	// the home directory folded back to "~". It is also what the title and the
112	// footer messages name the target.
113	//
114	// Both foldings answer the same pressure — this is the narrowest table in the
115	// application, and what a `nexus.example.com/docker-hosted/` prefix pushes out
116	// of the cell is the part that identifies the image. And both obey the same
117	// rule: the cache key stays the value everything else uses, so folding here
118	// cannot reach a loader, a scanner, or the directory a .gitleaksignore is
119	// written into.
120	func (t scanTarget) shortName() string {
121		if t.Kind == kindRepo {
122			return theme.FoldHome(t.Name)
123		}
124		if t.Display != "" {
125			return t.Display
126		}
127		return t.Name
128	}
129	
130	// secrets is the row's verdict. A row purged by ctrl+a no longer has a
131	// verdict either: its counters show `-`, and the icon says the same thing.
132	func (t scanTarget) secrets() theme.SecretsState {
133		return theme.SecretsVerdict(t.Sensitive, t.Scanned)
134	}
135	
136	// ci is the row's grade verdict, computed the way the workspaces list computes
137	// it — same function, same three absences. A purged row has no grade either:
138	// its counters print "-" and so does this column.
139	func (t scanTarget) ci() theme.CIScoreState {
140		return theme.CIScoreVerdict(t.CIScore, t.Scanned, t.CIGradeable)
141	}
142	
143	// misconfig is the row's misconfiguration verdict, computed the way the
144	// workspaces list and the images list compute theirs — same function, same
145	// three states. A purged row has looked at nothing: its counters print "-" and
146	// so does this column.
147	func (t scanTarget) misconfig() theme.MisconfigState {
148		return theme.MisconfigVerdict(t.Misconfig != nil, t.Scanned, t.Misconfig.Total())
149	}
150	
151	// labelFor names a target the way the table does, for the messages that have
152	// only a cache key to go on.
153	//
154	// It resolves the row rather than folding the string blind: an absolute
155	// repository path can legitimately begin with a configured registry URL, and
156	// only the row knows which of the two caches the name came from. A name with no
157	// row — nothing has been loaded yet — is returned untouched, which is worse
158	// than the alias but never wrong.
159	func (m Model) labelFor(name string) string {
160		for _, t := range m.inventory.Items() {
161			if t.Name == name {
162				return t.shortName()
163			}
164		}
165		return name
166	}
167	
168	// labelForResult folds a result's target the same way, for the one caller that
169	// has no inventory to resolve against: a view constructed straight onto a
170	// stored result. The result carries its own TargetType, which is the same fact
171	// targetKind holds.
172	func labelForResult(cfg *config.Config, result *scan.Result) string {
173		if result == nil {
174			return ""
175		}
176		if result.TargetType != scan.TargetImage {
177			return theme.FoldHome(result.Target)
178		}
179		return docker.ApplyAliases(result.Target, registryalias.From(cfg.Registry.Registries))
180	}
181	
182	// countColumnWidth holds the four severity columns to one width. datatable
183	// already reserves room for the sort arrow, which would give CRIT and HIGH six
184	// cells and MED and LOW five — four adjacent columns of the same kind, ragged.
185	const countColumnWidth = 6
186	
187	// countColumn builds one of the four severity columns. A purged row prints "-"
188	// rather than "0": nothing was found and nothing is known are different answers,
189	// and zero is the one a user reads as "clean".
190	//
191	// severity names the column's own level, for the colour. It is passed rather
192	// than derived from the title so that renaming a header cannot silently repaint
193	// a column — "CRIT" is an abbreviation, "CRITICAL" is the scanners' vocabulary.
194	func countColumn(title, severity string, get func(scan.SeverityCounts) int) datatable.Column[scanTarget] {
195		return datatable.Column[scanTarget]{
196			Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: countColumnWidth,
197			Cell: func(t scanTarget) string {
198				if !t.Scanned {
199					return "-"
200				}
201				return strconv.Itoa(get(t.Counts))
202			},
203			// Only a count that found something is coloured. Four columns of
204			// severity-coloured zeroes would be the whole table shouting at once,
205			// which says no more than a table with no colour at all.

213	// imageRows decorates the image list with the scan state the table shows,
214	// plus a placeholder row for any pull in flight whose image is not local yet.
215	func (m *Model) imageRows() []imageRow {
216		aliases := registryalias.From(m.registries)
217		// The scan frame comes from the registry, which holds the one chain that
218		// animates work (D5). spinnerFrameIdx below is local, and it animates
219		// loading — a load is not a job.
220		frame := m.jobFrame
221		scanning := m.scanningNames()
222		pulling := m.pullingNames()
223	
224		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(m.images))
225		rows := make([]imageRow, 0, len(m.images))
226		for _, img := range m.images {
227			raw := img.Name()
228			seen[raw] = true
229			entry, scanned := m.scanCache[raw]
230			rows = append(rows, imageRow{
231				Image:        img,
232				DisplayName:  docker.ApplyAliases(raw, aliases),
233				RawName:      raw,
234				Entry:        entry,
235				Scanned:      scanned,
236				Scanning:     scanning[raw],
237				Failed:       m.failedScans[raw],
238				Pulling:      pulling[raw],
239				SpinnerFrame: frame,
240				Update:       m.imageUpdate(img),
241				Signature:    m.imageSignature(img),
242			})
243		}
244		// An image pulled for the first time has no local row to spin yet — this
245		// is the common case when pulling from the registry browser, so it gets
246		// a placeholder rather than staying invisible until the pull completes.
247		for name := range pulling {
248			if seen[name] {
249				continue
250			}
251			rows = append(rows, imageRow{
252				DisplayName:  docker.ApplyAliases(name, aliases),
253				RawName:      name,
254				Pulling:      true,
255				SpinnerFrame: frame,
256			})
257		}
258		return rows
259	}

72	// misconfig is the row's misconfiguration verdict, computed the way the
73	// workspaces list and the security inventory compute theirs.
74	//
75	// An image has misconfigurations to find: `trivy image --scanners misconfig`
76	// reads the Dockerfile instructions baked into the layers, which is why this
77	// column is not repository-only the way the CI grade is.
78	func (r imageRow) misconfig() theme.MisconfigState {
79		return theme.MisconfigVerdict(r.Entry.Misconfig != nil, r.Scanned, r.Entry.Misconfig.Total())
80	}
81	
82	// misconfigColumn is the misconfiguration count. It exists only when
83	// scan.categories.misconfig is on — off, it would be a dash on every row — and
84	// it sits after the four CVE counters, before Scanned, which is where the
85	// workspaces list and the security inventory put theirs.
86	func misconfigColumn() datatable.Column[imageRow] {
87		return datatable.Column[imageRow]{
88			Title: "CFG", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: misconfigColumnWidth,
89			Cell: func(r imageRow) string {
90				return theme.MisconfigCell(r.misconfig(), r.Entry.Misconfig.Total(), r.Entry.Misconfig.UnrenderedCount() > 0)
91			},
92			Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
93				return theme.MisconfigStyle(r.misconfig(), r.Entry.Misconfig.WorstSeverity())
94			},
95			Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Entry.Misconfig.Total() < b.Entry.Misconfig.Total() },
96		}
97	}
98	
99	// cveColumn builds one of the four severity count columns.
100	//
101	// severity names the column's level for the colour, spelled as the scanners
102	// spell it — the title here is a single letter, which is no basis for deciding
103	// what colour a count is.
104	func cveColumn(title, severity string, get func(cache.ImageScanEntry) int) datatable.Column[imageRow] {
105		return datatable.Column[imageRow]{
106			Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 4,
107			Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatCVECount(get(r.Entry), r.Scanned) },
108			// A zero is dim, like an unscanned image: four coloured zeroes on a
109			// clean image would read as four findings.
110			Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
111				if !r.Scanned || get(r.Entry) == 0 {
112					return theme.DimStyle
113				}
114				return theme.SeverityTextStyle(severity)
115			},
116			Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return get(a.Entry) < get(b.Entry) },
117		}
118	}
119	
120	// scannedStyle colours the scan state, a failure being the one value in the
121	// column that asks for anything.
122	func scannedStyle(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
123		switch {
124		case r.Failed:
125			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
126		case r.Scanning, !r.Scanned:
127			return theme.DimStyle
128		}
129		// No opinion here: the table sets the theme's text color.
130		return lipgloss.NewStyle()
131	}
132	
133	// scannedCell reports the scan state: the spinner while one runs, an error icon
134	// when the last attempt failed, otherwise how long ago it succeeded.
135	func scannedCell(r imageRow) string {
136		switch {
137		case r.Scanning:
138			return r.SpinnerFrame + "scanning"
139		case r.Failed:
140			return theme.IconError + " error"
141		case r.Scanned:
142			return timeAgo(r.Entry.ScannedAt)
143		}
144		return "-"
145	}
146	
147	// imageColumns describes the Images tab. ID is the only column that neither
148	// sorts nor searches — twelve hex characters are not something anyone orders or
149	// looks for.
150	func imageColumns(withMisconfig bool) []datatable.Column[imageRow] {
151		cols := []datatable.Column[imageRow]{
152			{
153				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 14,
154				Cell: func(r imageRow) string {
155					if r.Pulling {
156						return r.SpinnerFrame + " pulling"
157					}
158					return shortID(r.Image.ID)
159				},
160				Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style {
161					if r.Pulling {
162						// In progress, no verdict yet — same treatment scannedStyle
163						// gives Scanning.
164						return theme.DimStyle
165					}
166					return lipgloss.NewStyle()
167				},
168			},
169			{
170				Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent,
171				MinWidth: 20, MaxWidth: 48, Flex: 1, TruncateHead: true,
172				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return r.DisplayName },
173				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return strings.ToLower(a.RawName) < strings.ToLower(b.RawName) },
174				// Both names. The filter has always matched the repository and tag
175				// docker reports; the alias the row actually shows was not
176				// searchable, which is a small thing that reads as a bug when the
177				// column says one name and the query wants the other.
178				Search: func(r imageRow) string { return r.DisplayName + " " + r.RawName },
179			},
180			updatecol.Column(false, func(r imageRow) imageupdate.Status { return r.Update }),
181			sigcol.Column(func(r imageRow) sigcol.State { return r.Signature }),
182			{
183				Title: "Disk Usage", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 12,
184				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatBytes(r.Image.UniqueSize) },
185				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Image.UniqueSize < b.Image.UniqueSize },
186			},
187			{
188				Title: "Content Size", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
189				Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatBytes(r.Image.Size) },
190				Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Image.Size < b.Image.Size },
191			},
192			{
193				Title: "Secrets", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: secretsColumnWidth,
194				Cell:  func(r imageRow) string { return theme.SecretsIcon(r.secrets()) },
195				Style: func(r imageRow) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SecretsStyle(r.secrets()) },
196			},
197			cveColumn("C", "CRITICAL", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Critical }),
198			cveColumn("H", "HIGH", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.High }),
199			cveColumn("M", "MEDIUM", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Medium }),
200			cveColumn("L", "LOW", func(e cache.ImageScanEntry) int { return e.Low }),
201		}
202		if withMisconfig {
203			cols = append(cols, misconfigColumn())
204		}
205		return append(cols, datatable.Column[imageRow]{
206			Title: "Scanned", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
207			Cell:  scannedCell,
208			Style: scannedStyle,
209			Less:  func(a, b imageRow) bool { return a.Entry.ScannedAt.Before(b.Entry.ScannedAt) },
210		})
211	}
212	
213	// imageRows decorates the image list with the scan state the table shows,
214	// plus a placeholder row for any pull in flight whose image is not local yet.
215	func (m *Model) imageRows() []imageRow {
216		aliases := registryalias.From(m.registries)
217		// The scan frame comes from the registry, which holds the one chain that
218		// animates work (D5). spinnerFrameIdx below is local, and it animates
219		// loading — a load is not a job.
220		frame := m.jobFrame
221		scanning := m.scanningNames()
222		pulling := m.pullingNames()
223	
224		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(m.images))
225		rows := make([]imageRow, 0, len(m.images))
226		for _, img := range m.images {
227			raw := img.Name()
228			seen[raw] = true
229			entry, scanned := m.scanCache[raw]
230			rows = append(rows, imageRow{
231				Image:        img,
232				DisplayName:  docker.ApplyAliases(raw, aliases),
233				RawName:      raw,
234				Entry:        entry,
235				Scanned:      scanned,
236				Scanning:     scanning[raw],
237				Failed:       m.failedScans[raw],
238				Pulling:      pulling[raw],
239				SpinnerFrame: frame,
240				Update:       m.imageUpdate(img),
241				Signature:    m.imageSignature(img),
242			})
243		}
244		// An image pulled for the first time has no local row to spin yet — this
245		// is the common case when pulling from the registry browser, so it gets
246		// a placeholder rather than staying invisible until the pull completes.
247		for name := range pulling {
248			if seen[name] {
249				continue
250			}
251			rows = append(rows, imageRow{
252				DisplayName:  docker.ApplyAliases(name, aliases),
253				RawName:      name,
254				Pulling:      true,
255				SpinnerFrame: frame,
256			})
257		}
258		return rows
259	}

content.content:
1	# Configuration — the schema and the view
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## Configuration System
7	
8	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
9	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `show_hidden_files`, `secret_backend`, `gauge_glyph`)
10	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
11	- `Forge` - the platform this context targets: `type`, URL and clone settings
12	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
13	- `Scan` - Security scanning: `categories` (what a scan looks for, and which
14	  tools run each one) and `tools` (one block per scanner — see `scanning.md`)
15	- `Network` - what the netdiag view runs on: the tool image, and the dials
16	  `internal/netcheck` used to hardcode; and `proxy_port` (8080), the one port
17	  every named forward route is served on (§3.74, see `network.md`) — at or above
18	  1024, and replaced by the default with a log line when it is not
19	- `MCP` - the read-only MCP server (§3.38): `enabled`, off by default, and
20	  `expose`, an allow-list of tool names
21	- `AgentUsage` - `agent_usage.prices`, the price table of the `:agent-usage` cost
22	  estimate (DEVDESK-47); no default, see below
23	
24	**`forge:` was `gitlab:`, and the rename is migrated rather than announced.**
25	A context targets one platform (§3.6), so the section is named after the role
26	rather than after the one implementation there was, and it gains a `type:` —
27	`gitlab` or `github`, **declared, never sniffed**, on the registry `provider`
28	precedent. An absent `type` means `gitlab`, which is what every file written
29	before the key existed meant.
30	
31	`migrateGitLabSection` runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, and that ordering is
32	the whole of it. Every default below writes into `cfg.Forge`, so a migration
33	placed after them finds a block that is no longer empty, takes the
34	field-by-field path, and silently drops the user's own `parallel_jobs: 7` — that
35	is not a hazard imagined for the comment, it is what the first draft did and
36	what `TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` caught. The other half of the
37	reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: `yaml.Unmarshal` is not strict here, so an
38	un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a context
39	at no host at all.
40	
41	**A whole-block copy when `forge:` is absent, field by field when both are
42	present.** The distinction exists for one field: `IncludeArchived` is a bool, so
43	"unset" and "deliberately false" are the same value and no per-field guard can
44	tell them apart — it can only be carried over when the new block says nothing at
45	all. When both are present the new one wins field by field: its values were
46	written later, and overwriting them with the old ones would undo the edit that
47	created the situation.
48	
49	`forge.type` is stated in `internal/config` and in each backend's `Shape()`, and
50	`TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheConfig` holds the two in step — config must not
51	import a backend, and a backend must not be the authority on what a config file
52	may say, so a test is the only thing that can. Same arrangement as the registry
53	`provider` names.
54	
55	The legacy secret migration is unaffected and the order is worth knowing:
56	`credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets` reads the **raw file** at router
57	construction, before anything can save, so a plaintext `gitlab.token` reaches
58	the store before the rename can rewrite the file without it.
59	
60	**`network:` was `docker:`.** The one key `docker:` held was never a Docker
61	setting, and the four other tabs of the configuration view are each named
62	after the section they write. That key — the image the OCI connectivity test
63	ran — has since been removed along with the feature itself; `NetworkConfig`
64	now holds only the netdiag dials (`CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`,
65	`CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`).
66	
67	**`scan:` was flat, and it is now `categories:` + `tools:` (§3.86).** Six
68	tools had grown three to five keys each, side by side with six `enable_*`
69	switches that named categories and tools interchangeably. `migrateScanSection`
70	(`scan_migrate.go`) runs right after `migrateGitLabSection`, before the
71	defaults, on the same model: field by field, only where the new value is empty,
72	the old keys held in `ScanConfig.Legacy` (inline, every tag `omitempty`) and
73	cleared so they leave the file on the next save. Two points of its own:
74	
75	- **The categories are carried whole or not at all.** A `categories:` block that
76	  is present is an answer, even all off; mixing it with the old switches would
77	  make one category's state depend on which file wrote it. The historical "all
78	  switches off means never configured" reading survives **only** inside the
79	  migration — the one place that still sees the switches. A file with no
80	  `categories:` at all gets `DefaultScanCategories()`; an empty tool list counts
81	  as absent, because a zero `Config` saves `tools: []`.
82	- **One change of meaning, on purpose.** `enable_k8s_schema` ticks kubeconform
83	  *and* helm and kustomize, which used to serve whenever installed and are now
84	  required: what is ticked is what the dashboard reports missing.
85	
86	A category's `tools` list is a slice, so a `Config` copied by value shares it:
87	`CategoryConfig.With` always builds a new one rather than editing in place.
88	
89	**`app.gauge_glyph`** picks the fill of the containers load gauges and of the
90	netdiag waterfall: `shade` (the default — `░` for fill and track alike, told
91	apart by colour) or `block` (`█` over a `░` track). `block` is an opt-in because
92	`█` is East Asian ambiguous width and overflows the gauge columns on a terminal
93	that draws it double-width. It is not derived from the locale: the locale says
94	how the process *measures*, not what the terminal *draws* (§3.96). It is applied
95	through `theme.SetGaugeGlyph` at startup, on a context switch and on every save,
96	and anything but `block` stays on the safe glyph. The setting also drives the glyph of the `:agent-usage` Breakdown bar
97	(`theme.GaugeFill`, in the agents table column and the Breakdown tab); `block` has
98	the same ambiguous width there, with the same accepted risk as for the gauges: a
99	line can overflow by one cell on a terminal that draws it double-width.
100	
101	**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
102	volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
103	`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
104	`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
105	external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
106	which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).
107	
108	`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
109	`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
110	configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
111	start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
112	held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
113	`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
114	cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
115	`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
116	views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
117	is still resolved.
118	
119	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
120	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
121	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
122	what makes the guarantee checkable.
123	
124	**`~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is not a context file** (§3.82). It holds whom to

# Configuration — the schema and the view

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## Configuration System

Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `show_hidden_files`, `secret_backend`, `gauge_glyph`)
- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
- `Forge` - the platform this context targets: `type`, URL and clone settings
- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
- `Scan` - Security scanning: `categories` (what a scan looks for, and which
  tools run each one) and `tools` (one block per scanner — see `scanning.md`)
- `Network` - what the netdiag view runs on: the tool image, and the dials
  `internal/netcheck` used to hardcode; and `proxy_port` (8080), the one port
  every named forward route is served on (§3.74, see `network.md`) — at or above
  1024, and replaced by the default with a log line when it is not
- `MCP` - the read-only MCP server (§3.38): `enabled`, off by default, and
  `expose`, an allow-list of tool names
- `AgentUsage` - `agent_usage.prices`, the price table of the `:agent-usage` cost
  estimate (DEVDESK-47); no default, see below

**`forge:` was `gitlab:`, and the rename is migrated rather than announced.**
A context targets one platform (§3.6), so the section is named after the role
rather than after the one implementation there was, and it gains a `type:` —
`gitlab` or `github`, **declared, never sniffed**, on the registry `provider`
precedent. An absent `type` means `gitlab`, which is what every file written
before the key existed meant.

`migrateGitLabSection` runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, and that ordering is
the whole of it. Every default below writes into `cfg.Forge`, so a migration
placed after them finds a block that is no longer empty, takes the
field-by-field path, and silently drops the user's own `parallel_jobs: 7` — that
is not a hazard imagined for the comment, it is what the first draft did and
what `TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` caught. The other half of the
reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: `yaml.Unmarshal` is not strict here, so an
un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a context
at no host at all.

**A whole-block copy when `forge:` is absent, field by field when both are
present.** The distinction exists for one field: `IncludeArchived` is a bool, so
"unset" and "deliberately false" are the same value and no per-field guard can
tell them apart — it can only be carried over when the new block says nothing at
all. When both are present the new one wins field by field: its values were
written later, and overwriting them with the old ones would undo the edit that
created the situation.

`forge.type` is stated in `internal/config` and in each backend's `Shape()`, and
`TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheConfig` holds the two in step — config must not
import a backend, and a backend must not be the authority on what a config file
may say, so a test is the only thing that can. Same arrangement as the registry
`provider` names.

The legacy secret migration is unaffected and the order is worth knowing:
`credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets` reads the **raw file** at router
construction, before anything can save, so a plaintext `gitlab.token` reaches
the store before the rename can rewrite the file without it.

**`network:` was `docker:`.** The one key `docker:` held was never a Docker
setting, and the four other tabs of the configuration view are each named
after the section they write. That key — the image the OCI connectivity test
ran — has since been removed along with the feature itself; `NetworkConfig`
now holds only the netdiag dials (`CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`,
`CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`).

**`scan:` was flat, and it is now `categories:` + `tools:` (§3.86).** Six
tools had grown three to five keys each, side by side with six `enable_*`
switches that named categories and tools interchangeably. `migrateScanSection`
(`scan_migrate.go`) runs right after `migrateGitLabSection`, before the
defaults, on the same model: field by field, only where the new value is empty,
the old keys held in `ScanConfig.Legacy` (inline, every tag `omitempty`) and
cleared so they leave the file on the next save. Two points of its own:

- **The categories are carried whole or not at all.** A `categories:` block that
  is present is an answer, even all off; mixing it with the old switches would
  make one category's state depend on which file wrote it. The historical "all
  switches off means never configured" reading survives **only** inside the
  migration — the one place that still sees the switches. A file with no
  `categories:` at all gets `DefaultScanCategories()`; an empty tool list counts
  as absent, because a zero `Config` saves `tools: []`.
- **One change of meaning, on purpose.** `enable_k8s_schema` ticks kubeconform
  *and* helm and kustomize, which used to serve whenever installed and are now
  required: what is ticked is what the dashboard reports missing.

A category's `tools` list is a slice, so a `Config` copied by value shares it:
`CategoryConfig.With` always builds a new one rather than editing in place.

**`app.gauge_glyph`** picks the fill of the containers load gauges and of the
netdiag waterfall: `shade` (the default — `░` for fill and track alike, told
apart by colour) or `block` (`█` over a `░` track). `block` is an opt-in because
`█` is East Asian ambiguous width and overflows the gauge columns on a terminal
that draws it double-width. It is not derived from the locale: the locale says
how the process *measures*, not what the terminal *draws* (§3.96). It is applied
through `theme.SetGaugeGlyph` at startup, on a context switch and on every save,
and anything but `block` stays on the safe glyph. The setting also drives the glyph of the `:agent-usage` Breakdown bar
(`theme.GaugeFill`, in the agents table column and the Breakdown tab); `block` has
the same ambiguous width there, with the same accepted risk as for the gauges: a
line can overflow by one cell on a terminal that draws it double-width.

**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).

`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
is still resolved.

**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
what makes the guarantee checkable.

**`~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is not a context file** (§3.82). It holds whom to
trust for image signatures — a fact about the world — so it is global, read by
`internal/trust`, and **strict** where `config.Load` is not: `KnownFields(true)`,
`version: 1`, and any error rejects the whole file (a typo would otherwise
weaken a rule in silence). It is edited by hand; the configuration view does not
touch it. Whether to verify at all is per context: `scan.image_verification`,
`on` or `off`, a string rather than a bool so a file written before the key
reads as `on` (D12) — and only `off` turns it off, so a typo verifies.

**`agent_usage.prices` — the price table of the cost estimate (DEVDESK-47).**
`internal/config/agent_usage.go`. DevDesk ships **no price**: the table is
written by hand in the context file, keyed by model name (kept exactly as
written; the matching rules are in `agent-usage.md`, "Pricing"). Each entry has
five rates, **all required**, in **USD per million tokens**:

```yaml
agent_usage:
  prices:
    claude-example-model:      # replace with the model id and the vendor's current prices
      input: 3
      output: 15
      cache_write_5m: 3.75
      cache_write_1h: 6
      cache_read: 0.3
```

The numbers above are an illustration of the shape, not prices to copy: take
the real ones from the vendor's price page. `0` is a valid explicit rate; a
missing rate is not 0, so an entry without all five keys is ignored (and logged),
which stops a forgotten `cache_read` from under-pricing silently.

- **`Rate` is tolerant.** A rate decodes through `config.Rate`, whose
  `UnmarshalYAML` never fails: an int or float is a number (`RateSet`), a
  missing key is `RateMissing`, anything else (`input: "5$"`, a list) is
  `RateInvalid`. A typo therefore costs **its own entry**, not the context:
  without this, a type error anywhere makes `LoadContext` fail with `failed to
  parse context`. An invalid value is kept as read and written back unchanged on
  save. `.nan`, `.inf` and negative numbers decode as values; rejecting them is
  `pricing.FromConfig`'s job, which logs `WARN [agentusageview]
  agent_usage.prices "<key>": <reason>` for each entry it leaves out.
- **No default, no migration, nothing written when empty.** `applyDefaults` and
  `Default()` do not touch the section, and a context with no prices saves
  without an `agent_usage` key. The format is user-written: renaming a key
  later needs a migration like `gitlab:` → `forge:`.
- **One block per context.** The section lives in the context file, so each
  context needs its own prices.
- **Not editable in `:cfg`.** There is no tab for it.
- **Read once.** The `:agent-usage` view reads the table when it is built:
  at startup, on a context switch and on `ConfigSavedMsg`. `ctrl+r` does not
  re-read it. **A save from `:cfg` rewrites the whole context file from the
  router's in-memory `Config`, so a hand edit made while DevDesk runs is
  overwritten by the next save** (comments in the file are lost on the first
  save too). Edit the prices while DevDesk is closed, or restart afterwards.

Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.

## Configuration view — `internal/ui/configuration`

114:### S-09 — Show each session's billed cost in the sessions list
115-Epic : E2 — Priorité : Should — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-97
116-
117-En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk, je veux voir le coût de chaque session dans la liste des sessions, avec une jauge relative à la session la plus chère et un tri par coût, afin de repérer les sessions les plus coûteuses sans les ouvrir une par une.
118-
119-**Critères d'acceptation**
120-1. Étant donné une session dont le transcript parent se termine par une ligne `cost-state` valide (`Billed.Known`), quand j'ouvre la liste, alors la colonne « Billed » affiche son total en USD (ex. `$12.61`, sans `~`).
121-2. Étant donné une session sans `cost-state` final, quand la liste s'affiche, alors la cellule indique `-` et aucune estimation n'est calculée.
122-3. Étant donné des transcripts de plusieurs centaines de Mo, quand la liste est chargée, alors seule une fenêtre bornée en fin de fichier est lue, jamais le transcript entier.
123-4. Étant donné au moins une session au coût connu, quand la liste s'affiche, alors chacune a une jauge proportionnelle à son coût sur celui de la plus chère (vert / orange / rouge, mêmes seuils que les jauges de la vue containers) ; sans coût, pas de jauge.
124-5. Étant donné la liste, quand j'appuie sur `.`, alors le cycle inclut Billed ▼ puis ▲, les coûts inconnus restant en fin de liste.
125-6. Terminal étroit : la jauge disparaît avant le montant ; Rule 116 tient ; la couleur n'est jamais le seul porteur.
126-7. Le Billed de la liste égale celui de l'en-tête du niveau agents ; aide `?` à jour ; exception à la Rule 122 déclarée dans le même commit.
--
166:6. La cellule « Est. cost » prend l'orange ou le rouge aux seuils de S-09 (en part du coût estimé total) ; rien n'est coloré sans au moins deux agents chiffrés.
167-7. Sous le curseur, l'information reste lisible sans couleur ; aide `?` à jour.
168-
169-**Hors périmètre** : teinte par famille de modèle (opus / sonnet / haiku : rien d'actionnable, Rule 122 « color discipline »), icônes dans la liste, animation, variante sans Nerd Font.
170-**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: l'icône d'état vaut surtout sur terminal étroit ; l'icône de type n'ajoute rien hors tri aplati.
171-**Questions ouvertes** : une ou deux colonnes d'icônes ; référence du seuil de coût (part du total ou de l'agent le plus cher) ; glyphes et rôles avec le ux-designer.
172:**Bloqué par** : S-09 pour le critère 6 uniquement.
173-
174-### S-12 — See a session's token rate over time as a sparkline
175-Epic : E2 — Priorité : Could — Effort : L (à redécouper : seaux M à L, affichage S à M) — Plane : DEVDESK-100
176-
177-En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk, je veux voir une courbe des tokens par minute d'une session, afin de repérer les pics et les temps morts.
178-
179-**Critères d'acceptation**
180-1. `internal/agentusage` expose des seaux d'une minute ; leur somme égale le total des tokens datés ; les messages sans horodatage sont comptés à part.
181-2. Un `message.id` répété n'est compté que dans un seau (ligne qui fait foi).
182-3. Le résultat incrémental égale la lecture complète (`FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull` étendu).
183-4. Le nombre de seaux est borné ; horodatages hors ordre ou futurs sans effet sur les autres seaux.
184-5. Une sparkline à la largeur disponible s'affiche sans changer la hauteur de l'en-tête ni du pied de page ; `-` sans horodatage.
--
